title: Learning Sparse Quantum States
summary: We study the problem of tomography for $k$-sparse quantum states. In contrast to classical distribution learning, where tight sample and time complexity bounds in terms of support size are well understood, no non-trivial bounds were previously shown for this problem. We give the first near optimal algorithm for learning $n$-qubit $k$-sparse pure quantum states, obtaining fidelity at least $1-\varepsilon$ with high probability using $\tilde{O}(k/\varepsilon)$ copies of the state and $\tilde{O}(kn/\varepsilon)$ time.
